The single biggest friction in week 1 of any R course is **getting students' machines into a working state**. Posit Cloud bypasses that entirely: students click a link and get a pre-configured RStudio in their browser, with every package the course needs already installed.

This page bundles a ready-to-upload template that takes ~10 minutes of instructor setup and ~30 seconds of student setup.

::: {.callout-tip title="When this is worth doing"}

- **Large classes** (50+) where install support consumes TA office hours
- **Diverse devices** (mix of Windows / Mac / Chromebooks / phones — Posit Cloud works on all)
- **Compressed terms** (summer / intersession) where week-1 friction means missing the term
- **Online sections** where you can't walk a student through a local install
- **First-time R students** who otherwise drop the course from setup frustration alone
:::

## Download the template bundle

[Download the template files](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/tree/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud) — five files, ~6 KB total:

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`setup.R`](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/blob/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud/setup.R) | Installs every CRAN + GitHub package the course uses |
| [`welcome.qmd`](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/blob/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud/welcome.qmd) | Sample first notebook for students |
| [`moderndive-template.Rproj`](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/blob/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud/moderndive-template.Rproj) | RStudio project file |
| [`.Rprofile`](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/blob/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud/.Rprofile) | Sensible R defaults; startup message |
| [`README.md`](https://github.com/moderndive/ModernDive_book/blob/v2-quarto-html/instructor-solutions/posit-cloud/README.md) | Detailed setup walkthrough |

## Instructor setup (one time, ~10 minutes)

1. **Sign up** for [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/). If your institution qualifies, request the [Cloud for Teaching](https://posit.cloud/learn/guide#account-types) tier — it's free for educators.
2. **Create a workspace** for your course (name it like "STAT 101 — Spring 2026").
3. **New project → RStudio Project**.
4. **Upload all 5 template files** (drag-and-drop into the Files pane).
5. **In the R console**: `source("setup.R")` — wait ~5 minutes for everything to install.
6. **Open `welcome.qmd` and click Render** to confirm the install worked.
7. **Project Settings → "Make Template"**. Posit Cloud freezes it.
8. **Share the workspace URL** (or just the project URL) with students.

## Student experience (no setup)

1. Student clicks the workspace URL the instructor shared.
2. "Save as Permanent Copy" → they get their own clean copy in their account.
3. Open `welcome.qmd`, run the first chunk: `library(palmerpenguins); glimpse(penguins)`.

That's it. They're coding within 30 seconds of clicking the link.

## Maintenance

| Trigger | What to do |
|---|---|
| Course adds a new package | Edit `setup.R` `cran_packages` or `github_packages`, re-source, click "Update Template" |
| Book updates GitHub-only datasets | Re-source `setup.R` in the template; click "Update Template" |
| New semester | Copy template into a fresh workspace named for the term; share the new URL |

## Tradeoffs vs. local install

| | Posit Cloud template | Local install |
|---|---|---|
| **Student setup time** | ~30 seconds | 30-90 minutes (varies wildly) |
| **Works on Chromebook / phone / school iPad** | ✓ | ✗ |
| **Needs internet during class** | ✓ (always) | ✗ |
| **Usage cap** | Free tier: 25 hours/student/month | ∞ |
| **Cost** | Free for educators (Posit Teaching tier) | Free (R + RStudio are free) |
| **Files survive between sessions** | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Can install one-off packages** | Limited (CRAN works; GitHub via `remotes` works) | ∞ |
| **Easy to share work with classmates** | Project link | Send `.qmd`, hope they have R |
| **What grader sees** | Same as student (rendered .qmd) | Same as student (rendered .qmd) |

Most courses use the template for **week 1-4** (when local-install pain blocks adoption) and let students transition to local installs later. Both can co-exist — the same `.qmd` files work in both environments.

::: {.callout-note title="If your institution has a Shiny Server / JupyterHub already"}
You may have a local equivalent. Check with IT before signing up for an external service. The pedagogical pattern (zero-install student workspaces) is what matters; Posit Cloud is one good vendor.
:::
